NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.CHOOSE_THE: Choose the Agent that should handle the request.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.TEST_THE_N: Test the node with representative input before using the result in later steps.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.THE_AGENT_: The agent list is loaded from the current project, so the selected project affects which agents are available.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.THE_NODE_C: The node calls the agent once for each input item.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.THE_NODE_S: The node stores agent identifiers behind the scenes when you select an agent; reselect the agent if you move or recreate it.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.THE_OUTPUT: The output is the message returned by the agent chat response. If the agent call fails, the output is empty and no error is raised.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.USE_THIS_N: Use this node to send a message into one of the project's AI agents and continue the workflow with the agent result.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_AI_AGENT_V1.WRITE_THE_: Write the Input message the agent should receive. You can include expressions from the current item or earlier nodes.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.FOR_GET: For Get, review the selected Fields and remove fields you do not need.
For Get, Update, or Delete, add filters that narrow the records. For Insert or Update, fill the field mapping values.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.FOR_GUI: For guided mode, turn Raw Query Mode off, select a Collection, then choose Get, Insert, Update, or Delete.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.GUIDED_: Guided field mappings are converted using the selected collection schema where possible.
Guided Get returns one output item per returned record when the response contains an items array.
Guided Insert, Update, and Delete return an action result with status and item information.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.IF_AUTH: If authentication is needed, choose Client Credential and select an active credential, or Blocks Authentication to use the run's delegated token (or the caller's own token if there is none; if neither exists, no token is sent).
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.KEEP_RA: Keep Raw Query Mode on for a direct GraphQL request, then enter the query or mutation in Raw Query.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.RAW_QUE: Raw Query is recommended for new nodes.

Raw Query runs once for each input item, and expressions in the query are resolved before it is sent. {{$json.field}} reads a field of the current item (same as {{$json.output.field}}); values inside "…" strings are escaped automatically.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.SELECTI: Selecting a collection can auto-populate schema fields and reset filters, field mappings, and selected get fields.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_DATA_ACTION_V1.USE_THI: Use this node to read or change records through Data Gateway. New configurations should use Raw Query mode, while the guided collection fields remain available for existing flows.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.A_FUNCTION_ST: A Function step with nothing wired into it still runs once when tested on its own, with no input.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.CHOOSE_THE_IN: Choose the Input: "Previous step's output" forwards the incoming item unchanged; "Custom JSON" opens an editor where you compose the payload, inserting values from earlier steps with {{ }} placeholders. {{$json.field}} reads a field of the incoming item (same as {{$json.output.field}}); values inside quotes are escaped automatically.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.INVOKES_A_DEP: Invokes a deployed Function synchronously and uses its returned value as this step's output.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.IN_CUSTOM_JSO: In Custom JSON mode, an input that is not valid JSON after the values are filled in fails the step before the function is called.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.ONE_INVOCATIO: One invocation per input item — a run that does not succeed fails the whole step.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.PICK_A_FUNCTI: Pick a Function. Only Live (deployed) functions are listed, and not always all of them. One whose workflow trigger is turned off is shown greyed out — turn that trigger on in the function's own Triggers settings before selecting it.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.TEST_THE_WORK: Test the workflow and confirm the function's returned value maps into later steps as expected.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.THE_FUNCTION_: The function runs with the caller's identity when the trigger has one. Schedule and email triggers have no caller.
The function's run is recorded under the function itself, triggered by this workflow execution.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_FUNCTION.THE_STEP_WAIT: The step waits for the function's own timeout plus a short grace. There is nothing to configure here.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.BODY_E: Body editing is only shown after Send Body is enabled and the body content type is JSON.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.CHOOSE: Choose the request Method and enter the target URL. Expressions in the URL are resolved for each input item.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.HEADER: Headers and query parameters are omitted unless their switches are enabled.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.IN_THE: In the JSON body, {{$json.field}} reads a field of the current item (same as {{$json.output.field}}). Values inside quotes are escaped automatically; without quotes a value keeps its type. A body that is not valid JSON after the values are filled in fails the step.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.OPTION: Optionally pick Authentication: Blocks Authentication uses the run's delegated token, or the caller's own token if there is none (if neither exists, no token is sent). Client Credential exchanges an IAM credential.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.TEST_T: Test the request and confirm the response shape before mapping it into later nodes.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.THE_NO: The node sends one request for each input item.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.THE_RE: The response body must be valid JSON. A JSON array response becomes multiple workflow output items.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.TURN_O: Turn on Send Body for methods that need a JSON payload, choose JSON, and enter a valid body.
Turn on Send Headers for authentication, content negotiation, or other request headers. Header names and values can use expressions. A manually set Authorization header is not overwritten.
Turn on Send Query Parameters if the endpoint expects URL query values, then add the key-value pairs. Keys and values can use expressions.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_HTTP_REQUEST_V1.USE_TH: Use this node to call an external HTTP endpoint from the workflow. It can send query parameters, headers, and a JSON body when those sections are enabled.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.A_JSON_ARRAY_RES: A JSON array response becomes multiple workflow output items.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.A_PATH_PARAMETER: A path parameter fills one segment, so it cannot contain a '/'. The node reports that rather than calling an endpoint the route does not declare.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.CALLS_ARE_RECORD: Calls are recorded in that proxy's execution log, marked as coming from a workflow and carrying the workflow, run and node.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.CHANGING_THE_PRO: Changing the proxy clears the endpoint, and changing the endpoint clears its path parameters.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.FILL_IN_ANY_PATH: Fill in any Path parameters the endpoint declares. Each one fills a single {name} segment and accepts expressions.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.IF_THE_ENDPOINT_: If the endpoint filters its response, the node only sees the fields it keeps.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.IN_THE_BODY_JSON: In the body, {{$json.field}} reads a field of the current item (same as {{$json.output.field}}). Values inside quotes are escaped automatically; without quotes a value keeps its type. A body that is not valid JSON after the values are filled in fails the step.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.ONLY_ENDPOINTS_O: Only endpoints on the proxy's allowlist can be called; anything else is refused by the gateway.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.PICK_THE_ENDPOIN: Pick the Endpoint. The list is the proxy's declared route allowlist, shown as method and path.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.PICK_THE_PROXY_O: Pick the Proxy. Only enabled proxies are listed.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.RUN_THE_WORKFLOW: Run the workflow and confirm the response shape before mapping it into later nodes.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.THE_NODE_CALLS_T: The node calls the proxy in-process, so no bearer token or tenant key is needed.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.THE_NODE_SENDS_O: The node sends one request for each input item. With nothing wired into it, it sends exactly one — so a proxy node on its own can be run with Execute Step.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.THE_PROXY_S_OWN: The proxy's own configured query values win over a query parameter set here when both use the same key.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.TURN_ON_SEND_BOD: Turn on Send Body for POST, PUT or PATCH endpoints and enter a JSON body.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.TURN_ON_SEND_QUE: Turn on Send Query Parameters if the endpoint takes a query string.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_PROXY.USE_THIS_NODE_TO: Use this node to call an endpoint through a proxy configured in the Proxy module. The upstream URL, the injected headers and credentials, and any response filtering all stay in the proxy, so the workflow never holds a third-party key.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.ATTACHMEN: Attachments left blank, or that resolve to an empty/unresolvable expression, are silently skipped - no error is raised for those entries.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.CHOOSE_TH: Choose the Language version of that template.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.ENTER_THE: Enter the recipient in To Email. You can use an expression when the recipient comes from the input item.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.OPTIONALL: Optionally add one or more Attachments. Each entry can be a literal storage File ID, or an expression such as {{$json.fileId}} or {{$node["NodeName"].json.output.fileId}} that resolves to one.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.SELECT_TH: Select the Template you want to send.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.TEMPLATE_: Template and language options are loaded from the current project.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.TEST_WITH: Test with a safe recipient or sample data before enabling it in a live path.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.THE_BODY_: The body mapping keys are derived from the selected template body, so changing the template can change which mappings are shown.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.THE_NODE_: The node sends one email for each input item.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.THE_OUTPU: The output also includes AttachmentCount and AttachmentsSent: the attachment entries after expressions are resolved, blank ones included. If sending throws an error, the output is an error item instead.
The output includes Success, Errors, and To so later nodes can inspect the send result.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.USE_MAP_B: Use Map (Body) to provide values for the dynamic keys found in the selected template body. Mapped values can also use expressions.
NODE_GUIDE_ACTION_SEND_MAIL_V1.USE_THIS_: Use this node to send an email from a project email template. The node asks for the template, language, recipient, and values for any dynamic template keys.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.ADD_THE_CONDITION: Add the conditions that should be evaluated against data from earlier nodes.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.AN_ITEM_WHOSE_CON: An item whose condition cannot be evaluated (for example, an unknown operator or one that does not fit the type) fails the step.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.CONDITION_VALUES_: Condition values are resolved as expressions before comparison.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.CONNECT_THE_FOLLO: Connect the following nodes to the appropriate branch for the result you expect.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.EMPTY_OR_INCOMPLE: Empty or incomplete conditions may not route the workflow the way you expect, so test both passing and failing cases.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.EQUALS_ONE_OF_LIS: Equals one of (list) checks that the value exactly equals one entry of the list (case-sensitive). All values are in (list) checks that every value of the left list is in the right list. Write the list as a JSON array or comma-separated values. An empty list makes these false, and their "not" versions true.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.NUMBER_BOOLEAN_DA: Number, boolean, date/time, and array comparisons are parsed by the selected condition type.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.THE_NODE_STARTS_W: The node starts with All conditions (AND) and no conditions.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.USE_ALL_CONDITION: Use All conditions (AND) when every condition must be true.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.USE_ANY_CONDITION: Use Any condition (OR) when one matching condition should be enough, then test both branches with sample data.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_IF_V1.USE_THIS_NODE_TO: Use this node to choose a workflow path based on conditions. Each input item is evaluated separately and then sent unchanged to either the true or false branch.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.ADD_ONE_ROUTI: Add one routing rule per output. Rules are checked from top to bottom and the item goes to the first one that matches.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.AN_ITEM_WHOSE: An item whose conditions cannot be evaluated fails the step.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.A_VALUE_THAT_: A value that is not a valid number, date or true/false makes its condition not match.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.CHOOSE_WHAT_H: Choose what happens to items that match no rule: drop them, send them to an extra Fallback output, or send them to one of the rules' outputs.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.CONDITIONS_WO: Conditions work exactly like the If node, with the same types and operators. Text comparisons are case-sensitive.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.CONNECT_THE_F: Connect the following nodes to the outputs.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.IN_EACH_RULE_: In each rule, pick the type and operator, then the value to compare with. Use AND or OR to choose whether all conditions or any one must be true.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.RENAMING_OR_D: Renaming or deleting an output never moves the connections of the other outputs. Deleting an output removes its connections.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.TURN_ON_RENAM: Turn on Rename Output to give an output a name. Without a name it shows its number: 0, 1, 2.
NODE_GUIDE_LOGIC_SWITCH_V2.USE_THIS_NODE: Use this node to send each item to one of many paths. Every output has its own conditions.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.ADD_A_FIELD: Add a field to every item (keeps item links):
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.ADD_A_VALUE: Add a value from an earlier node:
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.ALL_ITEMS: <0>$items</0> is the list of input items. Each entry wraps its data in <1>json</1>, so read fields as <2>$items[0].json.name</2> or <3>item.json.name</3> inside <4>map</4>/<5>filter</5>.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.ALL_NODE: <0>$node["Node name"]</0> gives access to all items of any earlier node:
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.ALL_WRAPPED: Items returned by these functions are wrapped in <0>json</0> too: <1>$node["Webhook"].first().json.email</1>.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.A_NEW_OBJEC: A new object without <0>__id</0> (a total, for example) is linked to <1>all</1> input items. It still works, but when those inputs came from different earlier items, later nodes read values from those earlier nodes as empty. Add <2>__id: $items[0].json.__id</2> (or the id of the item it belongs to) to pick one.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.BUILD_A_NEW: Build a new object from the current item:
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.CODE_RUNS_I: Code runs in a sandbox for data transformation, so external API calls, file access, package imports, and system commands are not available.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.EACH_JSON: <0>$json</0> is the current item's data. Read fields directly: <1>$json.name</1>. <2>$item</2> is the same value.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.EACH_NODE: <0>$node["Node name"].json</0> is the item from an earlier node that <1>this</1> item came from, for example <2>$node["Webhook"].json.email</2>.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.EXISTS_ONLY: <0>$json</0> exists only in each-item mode. <1>$items</1> and the <2>.all()</2> functions exist only in all-items mode.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.IF_THE_SCRI: If the script returns nothing or an empty array, the node produces no output items.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.LINKS_ALL_I: <0>All-items mode</0> links by the hidden <1>__id</1> field that every input item carries in <2>item.json.__id</2>. Returning <3>item</3>, <4>item.json</4>, or <5>{ ...item.json, ... }</5> keeps it. The field is removed from the saved output.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.LINKS_INTRO: Every output item remembers which input item it came from. Later nodes use that link to resolve expressions such as <0>{{$node["Webhook"].json.output.email}}</0> for the right item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.MATCH_ITEMS: Match items against another node's list:
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.MISSING_NOD: A node that produced no items, or that is not part of the current item's path, is missing from <0>$node</0>. Use <1>?.</1> when unsure: <2>$node["Webhook"]?.json?.email</2>.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.NOTE_EACH_I: In each-item mode, an error in one item does not stop the node. That item's output becomes <0>{ error: true, message }</0> and the remaining items still run. In all-items mode, an error fails the node.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.N_0_EACH_IT: <0>Each-item mode</0> links every output to its input automatically.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.RUN_THE_NOD: Run the node with real upstream data and check the output before connecting later nodes.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.STEP_MODE: Choose a <0>Mode</0>. <1>Run Once for Each Item</1> runs the script separately for every input item and is the simplest choice for per-item changes. <2>Run Once for All Items</2> runs the script a single time with the whole input list, for filtering, totals, grouping, or lookups across items.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.STEP_READ: Read input data with the variables for your mode (see <0>Variables by mode</0> below). Write JavaScript directly. Expression syntax such as <1>{{$json.name}}</1> does not work inside the script.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.STEP_RETURN: End the script with <0>return</0>. Return an object to produce one item or an array of objects to produce several items. Return <1>[]</1> to produce no items.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.THE_SAME_FI: The same field is written differently in expression fields and in code:
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.USE_A_VALUE: Use a value from an earlier node on every item:
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.USE_THIS_NO: Use this node to reshape, filter, combine, split, or calculate workflow data with JavaScript. Whatever the script returns becomes this node's output items.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_CODE_V1.YOU_CAN_REA: You can read any node that runs before this one, not just the node directly connected to it. Use the node's name exactly as it appears on the canvas (names are case-sensitive).
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_LIMIT_V2.CHOOSE_IN_: Choose in Keep whether to keep the first items or the last items.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_LIMIT_V2.EACH_KEPT_: Each kept item keeps its original item as its parent, so $node["…"] expressions in later nodes still refer to the original item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_LIMIT_V2.ENTER_MAX_: Enter Max Items, the largest number of items to keep. It must be a whole number, 1 or more.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_LIMIT_V2.IF_THERE_A: If there are no more items than Max Items, all of them go out.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_LIMIT_V2.KEPT_ITEMS: Kept items keep their input order in both modes.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_LIMIT_V2.LIMIT_RUNS: Limit runs once over all input items, not once per item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_LIMIT_V2.USE_THIS_N: Use this node to keep at most a set number of items, from the start or the end of the list.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.AN_INPUT_T: An input that receives nothing (an untaken If branch, or a step that output no items) has no data. With All, Merge then outputs nothing; with Any, that input adds no items.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.CHOOSE_RUN: Choose Run When: All outputs only when every connected input has data; Any outputs whatever arrived.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.CONNECT_TH: Connect the next node to the output.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.EACH_ITEM_: Each item keeps the item it came from as its parent, so $node["…"] expressions in later nodes still refer to its own branch.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.IF_NO_INPU: If no input receives any items, Merge outputs nothing and the next node does not run.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.LOWERING_N: Lowering Number of Inputs removes the connections on the inputs that are removed.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.MERGE_WAIT: Merge waits until every branch that can still run has finished, then runs once.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.SET_NUMBER: Set Number of Inputs (2 to 10), then connect one branch to each input.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_MERGE_V2.USE_THIS_N: Use this node to combine the items of several branches into one list. Append outputs the items of Input 1, then Input 2, and so on.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.BY_DEFA: By default, other input fields are not included.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.CHOOSE_: Choose Manual Mapping to add fields one by one, or JSON to enter an output object directly.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.FIELDS_: Fields you set are merged on top of the included input fields, so a new value can replace an included field with the same name.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.IN_JSON: In JSON mode, enter a valid JSON object. Expressions inside the JSON are resolved for each input item: {{$json.field}} reads a field of the current item (same as {{$json.output.field}}).
In JSON mode, values inside quotes are escaped automatically and values without quotes keep their type. JSON that is not valid after the values are filled in fails the step.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.IN_MANU: In Manual Mapping, choose the value type for each field so numbers and booleans are written as those types.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.SPECIFI: Specific include or exclude lists are comma-separated, so keep field names aligned with the incoming data.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.THE_NOD: The node runs once for each input item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.TURN_ON: Turn on Include Other Input Fields if the output should keep data from the incoming item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.USE_THI: Use this node to shape the output item by setting new field values manually or by providing JSON. It can also carry selected fields from the input item into the output.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SETFIELD_V1.WHEN_IN: When including input fields, choose All Fields, Specific Fields, or Exclude Fields.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.ADD_AN: Add another field to split several lists together.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.AN_ITE: An item without the field gives no items. After a run, the output shows which fields were not found in any input item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.AN_OBJ: An object is split by its values. A single value (including null) gives one item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.CHOOSE: Choose in Include which other fields of the input item each new item keeps: none, all, or only the fields you list.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.EACH_N: Each new item keeps its original item as its parent, so $node["…"] expressions in later nodes still refer to the original item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.IN_FIE: In Fields To Split Out, drag the field that holds the list from the input panel, or type its name, for example lines or order.lines.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.OPTION: Optionally, enter an Output Field Name to store each element under a new name. A name with dots, such as order.line, is written inside order.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.SEVERA: Several fields are combined by position: the first new item gets the first element of each field, and so on. A field that is not a list reaches only the first new item.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.TURN_O: Turn on Disable Dot Notation to read a key that contains a dot.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.USE_TH: Use this node to turn a list inside each item into separate items, so that the next nodes handle each element on its own.
NODE_GUIDE_TRANSFORM_SPLIT_OUT_V2.WITH_N: With No other fields, one field and no output field name, an object element becomes the new item itself.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.A_PAY: A payload that is not a JSON object is passed on as text.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.EACH_: Each event starts every published workflow that uses it, once per workflow.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.PUBLI: Publishing fails while the selected event is disabled for workflows. Disabling an event later stops its published workflows until it is enabled again.
Publish the workflow: only the published workflow runs when the event happens.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.REVIE: Review the output preview so later nodes can use the event's fields.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.SELEC: Select the Event to listen to. Only events enabled for workflows in this project are listed.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.THERE: There is no editor test run for this trigger yet.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.THE_O: The output holds EventId, EventName, SourceService, ConsumerName, IsMassConsumer, Timestamp and the event's Payload.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.TO_EN: To enable more events, use Manage events in the node notes; it opens the Event Triggers page in a new tab.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_BLOCKS_EVENT_V2.USE_T: Use this trigger to start a workflow when a Blocks service sends a platform event, such as a user change in IAM or a payment status in Utilities.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.A_CHA: A change runs matching draft workflows in test mode only when every record in it has a Tags array containing mock-data (Inserted and Deleted only; Updated changes carry no Tags). Other changes use published workflows.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.CHOOS: Choose the Operation that should start the workflow: Inserted, Updated, or Deleted.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.INSER: Insert and delete payloads include operation details, document id when available, timestamp, and document fields.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.IN_ED: In editor test mode, use data marked for test execution as described in the node notes.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.REVIE: Review the output preview so later nodes can use the fields this trigger provides.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.THE_X: The x-blocks-key is captured from the selected project.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.UPDAT: Update payloads include UpdatedFields with field name, old value, and new value instead of the full document fields.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_DATA_GATEWAY_V1.USE_T: Use this trigger to start a workflow when records in a Data Gateway collection are inserted, updated, or deleted.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.MAILBOX_OPTI: Mailbox options are loaded from the current project.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.MAKE_SURE_TH: Make sure the mailbox configuration is inbound-enabled, since only inbound configs are listed.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.MAP_FIELDS_F: Map fields from the trigger output into later nodes as needed.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.SELECTING_A_: Selecting a mailbox stores its mail server configuration id and x-blocks-key for the trigger.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.SELECT_THE_M: Select the Mailbox the workflow should monitor.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.THE_BACKEND_: The backend starts workflows only for inbound emails with received status.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.THE_PUBLISHE: The published workflow runs only while the draft still uses the same mailbox. If you change the mailbox in the draft, publish again.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.THE_TRIGGER_: The trigger output is the email event data passed into the workflow.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.USE_A_TEST_E: Use a test email to confirm the workflow receives the message data you expect.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_EMAIL_V1.USE_THIS_TRI: Use this trigger to start a workflow when an inbound email arrives in a configured mailbox.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.CHOOSE_A_: Choose a Trigger Interval: minutes, hours, days, weeks, or custom cron.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.CHOOSE_CU: Choose Custom (Cron) only when you want to type the 5-field cron expression directly.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.FILL_THE_: Fill the timing fields that appear for the selected interval, such as minute, hour, weekday, or day of month.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.HOURLY_SC: Hourly schedules use cron stepping, so intervals that do not divide 24 evenly run on matching clock hours rather than exact elapsed-hour spacing.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.PUBLISHED: Published schedule runs receive output fields such as WorkflowId, TriggerId, TenantId, CronExpression, and FiredAt.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.SCHEDULES: Schedules run on UTC time, so hours and the cron expression are in UTC.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.THE_SAVED: The saved parameters are normalized to triggerInterval and cronExpression; the helper timing fields are transient.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.USE_CRON_: Use Cron Preview to confirm the generated expression.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE_V1.USE_THIS_: Use this trigger to start a workflow on a time schedule. The guided interval fields generate a 5-field cron expression, and Custom lets you enter the cron expression yourself.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.CHOOSE_THE: Choose the authentication level: None for open webhooks, Blocks Authentication for signed-in callers, or Blocks Authorization when roles or permissions must be checked.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.CHOOSE_WHE: Choose whether the webhook should respond immediately or wait until the last node finishes.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.FOR_BLOCKS: For Blocks Authorization, choose the organization, authorization mode, and any required roles or permissions.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.IMMEDIATE_: Immediate response queues the workflow and returns a status quickly. After Last Node Completion waits for the workflow result.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.ROLES_AND_: Roles and permissions can require all selected values or any selected value, depending on the chosen condition.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.SEND_A_POS: Send a POST request with a JSON body and include the x-blocks-key header. A JSON object creates one workflow item, and a JSON array of objects creates one item per object. Other values (a plain string, number, or an array of them) are rejected. The header name is case-insensitive.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.THE_DEPREC: The Deprecated Webhook URL still works and embeds the x-blocks-key value in the path, so it does not need the header. Prefer the Webhook URL for new integrations.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.THE_TEST_U: The test URL only works while the workflow is listening for test executions. The production URL requires a published workflow.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.USE_THE_WE: Use the Webhook URL: Test while building the workflow, or Production after the workflow is published.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.USE_THIS_T: Use this trigger to start a workflow when another app sends JSON to the webhook URL. The incoming body becomes the data passed to the next node.
NODE_GUIDE_TRIGGER_WEBHOOK_V1.WHEN_WAITI: When waiting for the last node, Response Data controls whether the webhook returns all output items, the first output item, or no body.
